candidates.exact_span: The permittee must report total or total recoverable metal concentrations for compliance purpose.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether compliance comparisons must use total/total recoverable versus dissolved concentrations affects which reported measurement values are comparable to applicable numeric limits.

candidates.exact_span: Because State WQS for aluminum and copper were dissolved-based criteria, the linear partition coefficient for copper to convert dissolved copper concentration to total concentration is used to calculate the maximum daily effluent limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of whether and how the copper partition coefficient converts dissolved criteria into an enforceable total limit could change the numeric limit applied to reported copper measurements.

candidates.exact_span: However, because a partition coefficient for aluminum is not available, the effluent limitation for total aluminum is based on the dissolved criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether aluminum limits are expressed or evaluated on a dissolved versus total basis could change which numeric limit applies and how measurements are compared.

candidates.exact_span: Three samples with hardness data were submitted and the average of these samples 187 mg/L was used for RP screening purposes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: The hardness value used in RP screening may affect derived numeric limits for hardness-dependent parameters, changing which limit is applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: The permit proposes to continue to include monitoring for hardness (CaCO3) for later RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether hardness monitoring is an actually applicable FY2025 obligation versus deferred analysis could change whether monitoring was required during the evaluation period.

candidates.exact_span: Aluminum did show RP, however because the prescribed daily and 30 day average limit concentration (3.2 mg/l) is less stringent than the limit in the previous permit, the previous limit will be maintained at the request of NMED and to comply with antibacksliding requirements.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether the operative aluminum limit is the newly calculated 3.2 mg/l value or the antibacksliding-maintained previous limit changes which numeric standard is used for exceedance determinations.

candidates.exact_span: Permit limit of 0.75 mg/l daily max was previously established for aluminum based on water quality standards.
candidates.computation_change_reason: This establishes a specific numeric aluminum limit; interpretation of its continued applicability affects which enforceable limit is compared to reported measurements.

candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that the permit limit of 0.75 mg/l be applied to the 30 day average.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Applying a daily-max-derived limit to a 30-day average changes the applicable limit type and could change whether reported 30-day average measurements exceed the operative limit.

candidates.exact_span: Because aluminum exhibited RP, daily and 30 day loadings of 0.78 lbs/day will be established in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether mass-loading limits (lbs/day) are enforceable numeric limits in addition to concentration limits could change which limit applies and whether load-based exceedance comparisons are required.

candidates.exact_span: Copper did not show RP, however permit limit of .0011 mg/l daily max was previously established for copper based on water quality standards and will be maintained in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Maintenance of the 0.0011 mg/l daily max limit despite no RP could change whether a numeric copper limit remains applicable for compliance comparison.

candidates.exact_span: It is proposed that this limit be applied to the 30 day average as well.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Extending the copper daily max limit to 30-day average monitoring could change the applicable limit basis and exceedance evaluation for average results.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and discharge is infrequent, dissolved copper monitoring requirements will be maintained in the draft permit.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether dissolved copper monitoring remains required, and under what discharge-occurrence conditions, could change which monitoring obligations are applicable in FY2025.

candidates.exact_span: The permittee reported a non-detect result for Cadmium, however the testing submitted by the permittee did not satisfy SSM.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Whether a non-detect under non-SSM testing counts as adequate evidence versus a documented no-data or insufficient-evidence state could change missing-evidence classification.

candidates.exact_span: As previously described the permittee has not discharged in over five years and is unable to obtain a sample to analyze at the appropriate detection level.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A documented multi-year no-discharge period could establish that conditional monitoring was not required or that missing results reflect no discharge rather than inadequate evidence.

candidates.exact_span: As a result, the detection limit used by the permittee .002 mg/l was used as the effluent concentration value in RP analysis.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Use of the method detection limit as a stand-in effluent concentration for RP analysis could affect whether numeric limits are derived or prescribed, and whether reported non-detects support a compliance comparison or remain unresolved missing evidence.

candidates.exact_span: Only one sample result was provided as a result of a drought.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Interpretation of drought-limited sampling as a documented no-data condition versus insufficient evidence for required monitoring could change the missing-evidence state assigned to cadmium.

candidates.exact_span: Because data is limited and based on presumptive values, Cadmium monitoring and reporting requirements will be added to the draft permit to obtain more current data for later RP analysis. Limits will not be prescribed.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Addition of cadmium monitoring without prescribed limits affects whether numeric compliance comparison applies (A), whether cadmium monitoring is newly required (B), and whether absent results reflect report-only obligations or unresolved required monitoring (C).

candidates.exact_span: EPA proposes to continue to maintain the oil and grease narrative "no visible sheen" limitation.
candidates.computation_change_reason: A narrative sheen standard may not support ordinary numeric exceedance comparison, changing whether numeric compliance evaluation is applicable for oil and grease.
